title: It's superior to v2.  It is.
content: It seems to cue up in the app faster than v2, the night vision also works extremely well. But I want to explain, since I see some people saying color night vision doesn't work.  No, it works...but you didn't follow the instructions.  Thus let me help you out. You see, "color night vision" is not actually night vision. What? I said color night vision is NOT actually "night vision". TO understand, you need to understand "light". Night vision works by using infrared light, which is seen by the camera lens (but not the naked eye).  That's why you can't use an IR light for a camera facing a window; it's just going to reflect itself. TO solve this, you could put an IR blaster outdoors, but pretty much all of them require hardwire power.  Which defeats the purpose since a baddie could just cut the power. Enter "color night vision" - which again is not night vision. Cameras, all cameras, have a sensor.  This sensor needs light - regular light.  It behaves very similar to your eye; you can't see things without light.  The more light, the easier it is to see things. However, sometimes you can't increase the light level, yet you still need to see objects. In camera tech this is done by way of ISO, which is essentially a setting that tells the camera to compensate for lighting conditions - you can make things appear "brighter" or "darker". So...you combine a larger sensor with a higher ISO, and what you get...is "color night vision". In other words, all the camera's doing is amplifying whatever ambient light is there in order to improve the picture. ...ah, I see it's clicking to you now. TO use color night vision, NIGHT VISION SHOULD BE OFF.  Not "on", not "auto".  OFF. I know this doesn't make sense due to the naming.  But trust me on this. If you leave it "auto" the camera will sense that there's not enough light and just go to regular night vision (which will be black and white because color is not perceived through IR lighting.  Remember, IR sensors can't see the full spectrum of color). If you turn it off, the camera will simply adjust ISO based on whatever lighting is there and that's what you get. Now, you have to be realistic.  If there's literally NO ambient lighting whatsoever - I'm talking pitch black, no stars, no moon, NOTHING - you might as well do regular night vision with IR.  Or just get some light in there.  It doesn't need to be a lot - the side of my house has a single Phillips Hue bulb set at the lowest and I get full brightness through color night vision. SUMMARY:  color night vision needs at least some light to actually work, AND you must turn regular night vision OFF.

title: AMAZING pictures and night image, sound is low and unrealiable
content: I wanted a cheap home monitoring setup, and this camera is an AMAZING VALUE.  for under 30 dollars you get a HD camera that is wireless (although powered with a USB cable) that can record continuously on a micro SD card (up to 32 GB). The V3 has great images, a decent frame rate, two way audio with an 80 db siren you can activate.  The night feature means that even without ANY light, you can clearly see things happening. The trick that Wyze does is give you 3 weeks of their cloud recording to spoil you with ready access to all recording, when without the paid subscription you only get a 12 second video every 5 minutes, which is stored for 14 days, which is not bad.  I'm getting used to the subscription bonuses and may well decide to spend the money to keep them.  For someone who is only interested in coming home to review what the cat did all day, you might decide not to spend the money on the subscription. If you choose to put an SD card into the camera it will record 24/7 (and delete the oldest footage when it gets full) but you have to remove the card to put it into a device to see the recordings.  If someone steals the camera AND the SD card you may be out of luck to see who did it. The subscription is only $1.25 per month per camera and you get unlimited cloud recording plus a bunch of notification features such as alerts when the camera hears Carbon monoxide or Smoke detectors alarms. The audio features of this camera are its weakest feature.  Crackly audio or dropout is common, and its best to place the camera where is has fewer walls for the wifi signal to pass through.  The V3 only transmits on a 2.4 ghz signal (which is better for passing through walls anyway, but if it's outside you can sometimes make a big difference in connectivity by shifting the camera a few feet.  The data on the camera image shows how much data is being sent at any given moment, and if you don't have a solid data connection the audio suffers. Also, the audio volume from the camera to whoever your are talking to is fairly low, so above a certain height and distance they won't be able to understand what you are saying.  If you mounted in at eye height by your door, visitors would probably not have a problem hearing you, provided the camera has a solid wifi connection. This camera has SUPER night imaging capability, and switches from black and white night mode to color night mode if it detects motion.  You set the detection level for each camera so that minor movements like branches waving in the wind don't result in unwanted alerts.  You can also set audio trigger thresholds depending on the environment.  My camera looks at a 60 watt light fixture and manages to not become totally blown out. Setting up the cameras is very easy, you install the app and create an account, then push the setup button under the camera and log into your wifi.  A code is sent to your registered email account that gives you control of the camera, and even offers an optional two-step login to prevent possible hacking of your system.  As it stands, even the single stage login feels pretty secure, but it's nice to have the option, which you can turn on later. Each registered camera appears on your app screen, and you pick the camera you want to look at or configure and tap on it.  managing 6 cameras is as easy as one camera, even if it seems repetitious to have to individually configure each camera separately. These cameras are made to work outdoors and are IP66 rated, so dust and moisture should not be a problem, but I do intend to protect mine by mounting them where they will have some overhead cover from the elements. If you want an inexpensive home monitoring system that doesn't actually require a subscription (though you will probably WANT the subscription) then I haven't seen anything that approaches the V3.

title: Great price but need improvements
content: I have a love/hate relationship with Wyze’s security cameras. I love the low cost of their cameras. It’s easy to install and setup. No subscription is required (but with limitations)! Live view, for the corded cameras, loads very quickly. I hate the significant notification delay when the camera detects motion. I’m talking about up to a minute delay (at times 2-3 minutes)!! So don’t expect to be able to speak with anyone through the camera because they’ll be gone by the time you get notified of their presence. I get a lot of false alerts. The camera detects “motion” from moving shadows and headlights at dusk. I live in the center of two busy streets so it’s difficult to aim the camera away from the passing cars on either side. At night, I’ll get notifications of every car that passes because of their headlights. During the day, adjusting the detection sensitivity reduces the amount of false alerts from cars. Error code 07 occurs a quote a few times which prevents video playback of an event. I also get missed motion detections. I had an amazon delivery today (March 26 at 10:18am) and 2 cameras failed to detect the driver. My last notification for the day was at 8am so it wasn’t caused by the “cool down” limit. The camera also has a short cord so you’ll need to purchase their extension kit if you don’t have an outlet within 5 ft of your installation spot. I also own 2 wireless outdoor cameras. One is installed on the side of the house without a nearby exterior outlet and the other camera is in front of the house on a tree that is roughly 15 ft from the house. Two weeks after installation, the battery percentage is at 80%. The live view loads a lot slower when compared to the wired cameras. It takes 15-20 seconds to load live view whereas the wired cameras load live view within 5 seconds.

title: So far so good
content: Got it on April 3, 2021. (Today is April 14, 2021.) So far so good. Installation: Very very easy. Following the instruction in the manual, I just connected the USB cable for power, installed a smartphone App, configured the app for connectivity, and put a MicroSD card. If you have any difficulty, ask Google (e.g., how to setup Wyze cam). You will see a few good helps including Y**t*be video clips. Regarding the video: On April 3, I put a 32GB MicroSDHD card (that was formatted with GUIFormat program available free on the Internet). I set the video quality to SD for continuous recording. Wyze generates one mp4 file for one minute. The 32GB card could hold 4-days SD videos. The SD video quality was good enough. Today, I put a 128GB MicroSDXC card (that was, again, formatted with GUIFormat program). The file system should be FAT32 (not exFAT nor NTFS). I first formatted the card to NTFS in Windows. Then, I formatted it to FAT32 with GUIFormat to avoid "currently-being-used error" of GUIFormat. Wyze Cam has had no issue with it. In order to extend the length of recordings in the card, I switched the quality to 360p (which is not much different from SD 480p). I have not checked the visual quality yet, but it should be not much different from that of SD. Regarding subscription: Though the cost of subscription is not much (around $15/year? for each cam), I decided not to subscribe the service. Since the device records continuously and the 128GB card can hold around 20 days records, I can refer to the recorded video files if needed. I mean, I can rely on the recordings instead of cloud. I will let you know later if the no subscription option is good OK. Hardware and software quality and durability: Again, so far so good. The device is a bit warm, but not hot. I hope the heat does not cause any trouble in the long run. So far, the device is working very well, continuously recording without any issue. The Android app/software is very good. I am sure iPhone app also functions well, too. I will report my experience several weeks later.

title: Great improvement over the v2!
content: I've owned multiple Wyze Cam v2's since 2018 and while they have worked wonderful since, the improvements in the new version (as well as the cost) persuaded me to upgrade. The improved camera sensor is literally a night and day difference. In cases where the cam v2 would switch on the infrared lights and go into "night vision" mode no longer occurs with the v3. The ability to choose between "near" or "far" IR lights is a bonus as well. One other major improvement over the v2 is the weather resistance rating. There is a short micro usb cable that is connected to the back and is permanently connected to the camera to seal it from the elements. On the other end of the cable is where you plug in the included power cable. This part of the connection is sealed by a rubber-like tip. Even the port for the SD card has a small cover. Good attention to detail. Setup is quite simple. Download the app, log in or create a Wyze account, select add device, and choose the correct product. The directions walk you through the rest. One thing I will point out is that you need to select a 2.4ghz Wi-Fi network. It may list your 5ghz network and the camera will tell you it couldn't connect. It might be useful if Wyze added some text to the network select screen mentioning that. EDIT: It appears the app now tells you. One point I like to mention to new possible buyers is that you should not rely on these or any other similarly priced camera's for security purposes. They are great for keeping an eye on things, but if you are solely looking for something to provide security you should be looking at spending a bit more.

title: The App doubles as monetization scheme
content: The entire app, required to use this product is a constant nag for you to give them a subscription fee for their cloud services. I also think the app is really confusing and it took me a while to actually understand how to set things up for sound and motion recording. I don’t know why there wasn’t included directions printed how to actually click on stuff and make things happen. Maybe because they redesigned the app so often I don’t know. They won’t stop telling me how awesome it is with all of the design and the user interface is specifically split between “plus” functions To show you what you’re “losing” if you don’t give them money every month. I also had no idea that you couldn’t record locally without an SD card I wish that somehow that was more obvious before I bought it. But I think they purposely don’t include one so they can try to upsell you in cloud storage and the physical product costs less. Call me old-fashioned but I would like to just use my product and not being nagged for money all the time. I wouldn’t recommend this product to anybody just for that reason alone. This product honestly is the worst of what a smart phone era has to offer. I’m sure the subscription BS is at least moderately effective and they make money ...but I think Just because you can make money doesn’t necessarily mean that it’s OK. I understand this model with FREE games/apps because you don’t pay for the entire thing. But consider some thing like iphone. When you purchase the physical product, it has local storage that comes with it and it tells you that you can do cloud services but it doesn’t consistently remind you all the time that you’re not paying them for cloud services. Every time you look at your pictures it doesn’t say “Hey you could have more space on your phone if you bought our stuff”. Something about the design of this makes me feel like part of it should be illegal. Because you’re paying for a product But still wasting your time being nagged. And the entire design is just a mental game to press you for more money. Yay capitalism. The actual camera and tech itself is pretty good. But honestly I’m just so sick of this type of crap. Needless to say I don’t think I want to buy any Wyze products. Somehow all of my other smart devices don’t seem to be advertising to me like this. Their apps focus on actual utility, not monetization gimmicks.

Location has DSL that often benchmarks at 250Kbps down and 80Kbps up, so can only turn on single camera or overload upstream bandwidth.  Camera comes on at SD then tells me network is unstable and i should switch to 360p mode - it was set to 360p until i turned it off and back on.  App or firmware??? Also, have to turn off all but 1 of the 10 cameras or network overload causes most to go offline until oower cycled.  Should be able to keep cameras enabled at HD but ONLY recording to local SD so they dont overload network upstream bandwidth.  AS IS, they are USELESS with low bandwidth connections. Another bug: DHCP timeouts because ubiquiti mesh network slow to configure after frequent power outages by PG&E. These could work much more reliably if static IP was an option.  Otherwise camera goes offline until next power outage resets then if lucky comes back online... Wish i could download firmware image to local NFS or SMB share or my phone and verify checksum then push to the multiple cameras, currently each camera fails firmware upsate 3-5 times before successful so to update all 10 cameras takes more than a day with all the retries. Have reported multiple firmware bugs on Wyze support forum without responses. Hopefully firmware will be fixed soon  V2 cameras took a lot of time to fet mostly stable. Hopefully Starlink service will  be offered soon to solve my DSL peoblems.  No other options for internet.

All apps should!!  don't let the hackers into your IoT because they stole or guessed your password!) - though it isn't token or authenticatorApp based...still way better than just a password. I read somewhere that the event captured videos used to go through China servers (though they were encrypted) but more recently I read that Wyze changed that so all video from US cameras stay in the US.  If that worries you, check into it - don't take my word on it. I also bought a Micro SD card (from Amazon of course) so the continuous video recording stays on the device (on the SD card):  SanDisk 32GB MAX Endurance microSDHC Card with Adapter for Home Security Cameras and Dash cams - C10, U3, V30, 4K UHD, Micro SD Card - SDSQQVR-032G-GN6IA  : https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B084CJLNM4/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o05_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 It holds about 4 days worth of continuous video in the camera.  The continuous video on the SD card is accessible via the app (and the app servers are in the cloud like everything else) but is supposed to be end-to-end encrypted. I think motion alerts are part of the subscription package ($20 a year per camera) but I'm not using those so I don't know for sure.  From what I could tell, all cameras are now charging a subscription fee.  There is no fee to record to the local SD card.  (The SD card has to be formatted FAT32 so Wyze claims the camera  can only support cards up to 32GB.  Some people online have said they managed to get cards as high as 128GB to work.  I don't know anything about that.  If that is important - then you should check into it). I liked the camera so much, that I just bought another one and it should be arriving any minute now!

title: Camera is EXCELLENT -- Wasserstein Floodlight mount leaves something to be desired
content: We needed to replace two outdoor motion-detecting floodlights with video surveillance, and the Wyze Cam v3 is perfect for the job.  This review is mostly about the Wasserstein "3-in-1" Floodlight for the v3 cameras. Wyze cams and the Wyze app are a breeze to pair and set up.  Picture quality is excellent as is the IR night vision.  The base is magnetic and the package includes a metal disc that can be mounted with either the included 3M double-sided tape or the included screw for more permanent attachment to facilitate surface placements.  The camera can also attach to one of two specific Wasserstein floodlights, but the floodlights are not without their flaws. The Wyze Cams v3s all come with an attached micro-USB cable (about 5 inches long) with female connector which is fully sealed with a silicone shroud to prevent water intrusion outdoors once a male connector is inserted, and it will do the job.  But the Wasserstein floodlight is made to work with a variety of USB connected cameras, so there is a generic USB-A female port on the housing.  That port is covered with a silicone cap to keep water out -- which it will do . . . IF YOU DON'T NEED TO PLUG IN A CAMERA.  So why would you buy that floodlight otherwise?  Once a cable is plugged in, the silicone cap is utterly useless.  I pulled it off and threw it away. Wasserstein doesn't include a shorty USB-A to micro-USB male connector (that could be weatherized to seal the power port) so you're stuck with having to do something with 5'10" of USB cable that comes with the camera to connect to the floodlight. The camera slips into a cheap plastic tray that screw onto a 1/4-20 mounting screw that swivels, but there is no way to actually secure the camera to the mount, so it is vulnerable to theft . . . the only deterrent being the height of the camera above ground level -- if tall enough, a person could jump up, grab the camera, and simply break the tray off the floodlight.  This is a serious design flaw.  They could have outfitted the fixture with a 90-degree mount that screws into the base of the v3 with the OEM stand removed. There are two versions of the floodlight, one with a remote to control light intensity, and sensitivity to motion and darkness.  Although the product photos for the remote make it appear as though there is ink on the markings to make them visible, as you can see in the photos (one from the user manual and one of the actual remote), the markings are virtually impossible to read, especially if you don't have good close-up vision. Don't hesitate to get the Wyze Cam v3 if you need outdoor surveillance -- it even has a LOUD siren that can be activated from the app!  Annual "Cam Plus" subscription is just $15 per camera (too bad they don't have volume packages -- I installed seven cameras in my mother-in-law's home so my wife can keep track of her, so that's $105/year).

content: After installing these at my house and using them for a few months here are the overall pros/cons I've experienced: Pros: At this price there is nothing better. Since they don't weigh much 1 screw is all that's needed per camera. They look modern/sleek. Video quality during the day and at night with is good (not excellent). Don't expect to be able to see any license plate numbers beyond 10 feet from the cameras because that won't happen. I'm glad users can turn off the very visible blue yes, blue light on each camera. Wyze...what the heck were you thinking when you chose that color? LOL...stick with what has and will forever look best for cameras...red status light! I'm in the central valley of California and temperatures have recently been near 100 and the cameras haven't had any overheating issues. Person detection and push notifications of persons detected works great and is worth the $2.00/per month per camera charge. I have the most entry level standard wifi plan with AT&T and person notifications arrive on my iPhone in about 10 seconds. Cons: Since only 1 screw holds these cameras they can easily be stolen in less then 5 seconds. Not joking. All it takes is one good pull and the camera + the sd card inside (if you put one in) are gone. With the exception of person detection that works great all other notifications (package, cars, motion etc) are ABSOLUTELY HORRIFIC. It doesn't matter what sensitivity setting you chose or what zones you have set if you don't turn OFF all these notifications (except persons) you'll be very upset with the detection capabilities. Wyze really needs to work on their zone and sensitivity settings. Setting zones and sensitivity levels is useless because even if something is out of the zone or on sensitivity level 1 (lowest) I still receive tons of false notifications. This is why I only have person detection on. It's really the only reason why I have a paid subscription. Overall...for the price I can't give this less then 5 stars and CNET, PC Magazine, Editors Choice etc agree. No other company is able to deliver a camera like this at the ridicoulously low price of $25/each. Note, that when these V3 cameras are sold out on the official Wyze site Amazon increases the price to $33 per camera.

title: It's always something with these cheap cams!
content: REVIEW UPDATE:  It always seems like there is SOMETHING with Wyze products!  I think the are so busy pushing out new, sub-par products that they never get anything fully "right".  I got a replacement for the dead cam through Amazon..... and now the other two are having issues!  I am using them with TinyCam Pro, in a "cloud" setup/setting.  First, if you update the firmware, they simply will not work at all with TinyCam, so had go through the hassle of reverting the firmware to make them work with TinyCam.  Then, every 3 minutes, each camera blanks out for approx. 5 seconds.  Sometimes the camera image pops back up, and other times when it does, TinyCam crashes.  I'm pretty tech savvy, and after looking at the code in the Wyze firmware update, it appears they have intentionally coded the firmware to make the cameras NOT function with anything other than the Wyze app.  Why make a substandard product when it could be so much more?  And why make such a sloppy app, that again, could be so much better??  Wyze is always on the verge of having a superior product for the money, but they always drop the ball in the end. FOLLOW UP:  One of the 3 cameras I received totally died on the 3rd day of use.  Amazon was great about returning it for a replacement, but that should not happen..... so my initial review has dropped from 3 to 2 stars. ORIGONAL REVIEW: This is what the original Wyze Cam should have been in regard to image clarity and night vision. The night vision is superior to any of the other Wyze cameras. I purchased 3 of these cameras on the same order, and there is an image issue with each.... that being that each camera has a different zone within the onscreen image that is out of focus compared to the rest of the image. (cleaned all the camera lenses after mounting)  One camera has an out of focus area in a strip that runs from the lower right corner of the image, to the upper middle.  Another has a horizontal strip straight across the middle of the onscreen image, and the third has the entire right side of the onscreen image out of focus. Another VERY annoying thing is that all of these camera go blank on the screen every 3 mins, for approx. 2 seconds, and then return to the image.  This happens like clockwork, with all three of the cameras I received. (I am using TinyCam Pro as the camera image/screen host.)  I found out the hard way that if you upgrade these, or any of the Wyze Cameras to the latest software version, they WILL NOT function with TinyCam Pro.  I had to download, and revert each camera individually to the old software in order for them to function with TinyCam Pro. These cameras are still likely the best bang for the buck in terms of affordable security cameras, but it feels like Wyze just does barely enough to eek by getting the cameras to sell. Although the advertising would have you believe otherwise, the only tangible thing you get for paying the extra money for the V3 cameras is the improved night vision, and that is almost offset by the annoyance of the image flash out every 3 minutes, and the out of focus areas within each camera's image.

content: I bought this (my 4th Wyze cam) mostly to do time lapse videos off a balcony overlooking the water.  I'm extremely disappointed with the quality of the realtime video, which looks like it's ruined by the compression.  I get chunky blocks instead of clear individual pixels.  Thinking that may be because of WIFI limitations, I tried taking some stills, and the chunk blocks didn't get any better. Then I did a couple of 12 hour time lapse videos, like I've done 100 times with my Wyze V2's.  The quality of the videos is much worse than the V2, they don't play back properly in the App, and I can't get them to download into Android (Windows emulator or native Android) like I did with the V2.  The camera just locks up.  With the V2, it locked up for a few minutes for the download.  With the V3, it never comes back and I have to restart the App, so I never get to see the time lapse videos Looking at the realtime videos on full screen and expanded, solid posts seem to move, when it's actually the water behind them that's moving.  And they're only 10' away.  Another compression artifact, I suspect.  I doubt I could identify a person on the videos, much less a license plate at 25'- ruling it out for any security/evidentiary purpose. Bottom line, I was marginally satisfied with my Wyze V2 cameras, less satisfied with my Wyze tilt, pan and zoom camera (which has the same blocky compression) and this V3 is pretty much useless.  I have cheap action cameras with absolutely superior resolution.  If only they had something similar to the Wyze app, which is pretty impressive. But it was only $30.

title: Great Value, Much Improved Night Vision
content: The retail for this camera direct from Wyze is $24 but they are charge around $5 for shipping. It's around $30 at all third party retailers. The original Wyze V2 camera was $20 retail and is still a fantastic camera for the price but the V3 adds some nice improvements that I think is  well worth the $4 (or even $10 in most places) price increase. For one, the V3 is now rated for use outdoors. It's IP65 weather & dust resistance. I'm not sure how it will hold up in the harsh northeast winters but I'll put it to the test and check back in a year. Their new sensor and ƒ/1.6 aperture allows for much better video capture at night. And I also like that they have now allowed for a built-in mini siren. It's not very loud but could be useful in a pinch to scare off intruders. The setup is just as easy as the V2 and it still retains many of the same useful features like customizable zone and sound detection, monitoring for smoke or CO alarm, free 12-second motion and sound event video recording to the cloud, time-lapse recording, and easy integration with Alexa, Google Assistant and IFTTT. The one major downside Wyze cams are that their cool off time for cloud recording is 5-minutes. That means that when there is continuous motion, the camera will only capture one 12-second event video every five minutes. You can add local storage and it will continue to record to that or opt in to their Cam Plus subscription for contentious recording to the cloud as well as a host of other benefits for $2/month.

Black and white night mode is better even though I have a streetlight above the area it films. But the requirement to subscribe and pay for person detection makes the wyze v3 an expensive proposition. If you haven’t had one of these cameras, person detection and notification is the killer app.  Especially because you can’t scrub at high speed through footage.  So without person alerts you are going to face the prospect of spending hours watching footage to find what you are looking for. I have a eufy 2k camera with person alert by the front door and if I had only one camera that would be it.  After some position adjustments to catch people walking sideways past, it is pretty reliable at detecting people (and free). The wyze v3 didn’t detect people quite as reliably. But the eufy in my experience only accepts a 32 Gb sandisk max endurance card while the wyze works with a 128 gb sandisk max endurance.  Ironically this is opposite of what they say they support; wyze is supposed to only support 32 while the eufy is documented to accept 128. Be aware that all these cameras capture very compressed data, like a hundred or two kbps.  They are no match for cell phone or gopros which give clearer images.

title: Best camera in it's class.
content: One of the best camera's in this price range. Setup is easy. The V3 camera has black and white night vision. It uses 4 infrared led's to provide lighting. If set standard, you will see the LEDs as red dots on the camera. If in low power mode, you will not. This setting is easy to change. In my garage at night, with all doors closed and lights off, you cannot see your hand in front of your face. The camera will see you just fine in low power mode as it illuminates the entire 2-car garage area with it's infrared. The V3 camera has a much better night mode than the V2, so make sure you are getting the V3. They also sell a spot light unit to illuminate the area for color if you need it. It will turn on the lights when it detects motion or sound. The power indicator on the camera can be turned off so an intruder does not see it. The camera is a 2 1/2" white cube with a small collapsible stand. The V3 camera is outdoor rated. The connector is about a foot down the wire, protected by a rubber boot. You can disconnect the provided usb cable here and attach a longer one. Be sure to keep slack so water will not run down the cable and short this connection. Where the cable goes into the camera itself is sealed so water will not ruin the camera. It will send alerts to your phone if desired. This is free with the camera. The resolution is 1080p, which is 2K.Night mode seems grainier, but still good. The phone will upload 12 second events to Amazon cloud (included with camera) or you can insert a 32gb Micro SD card to record more. If they steal your camera, they get your recorded video, but not the initial 12 second recording. Cord provided is 6' long. I found 25' foot cables for about $12 for 2. This allows more flexibility in mounting. The camera has a mic and speaker, do it will record sound. It has an alarm but it's not particularly loud but you can definitely hear it. You can also speak thru the camera from your phone. So you can give delivery instructions or scare off an intruder. Again, this is the most feature packed camera I have seen in the class. You could want better resolution, but 1080p is still a good quality image.

title: SUPER slow with Google Home/Assistant
content: I have a few Google Nest Hub Max displays set up in my home along with some Nest indoor and outdoor cams.  I wanted to expand my camera coverage area inside my home, so I decided to give these inexpensive Wyze 3s a try.  The Wyze cameras themselves have some nice features compared to my Nest cams (SD card ports, time lapse, color night vision, flexible mounting options, etc) that work great, but the feature that I cared about the most, which is the integration with Google Home/Assistant, is lacking.  While it does connect to Google Home as easily as Google's Nest cams, the time to first load the video on the Google Hub displays is VERY slow.  It takes around 2 to 3 minutes for the Google displays to load a live feed from the Wyze cam, while it takes less than 10 seconds for the same displays to load live feeds from the Nest cams. Loading Wyze live feeds on my iPad (on the same WiFi network as the displays) takes only a few seconds as well, which leads me to believe there's an issues with the Wyze <-> Google Home/Assistant integration.  If you're trying to catch something happening in real-time, you'll probably miss it and will have to resort to the recorded footage. I really hope that they fix this issue as I would love to purchase a few more of these cameras, at such a low price compared to Nest, but until this integration issue is resolved, the Wyze 3's only real use to me right now is as a nanny cam.

title: Good Camera, Poor Software Features, Shady Subscription
content: I should preface this review by saying that I almost never write bad reviews and that my expectations for this camera were low.  That said, given the price point (and favorable reviews) I honestly thought I'd be pleased with this. The camera is pretty amazing. Sure the detail could be better, but I have it mounted on a second story windowsill overlooking the backyard and our cars. I don't think it's enough to make a positive ID but I'm honestly quite impressed with the picture quality. The night vision is truly fantastic. For what I paid, it's great. On to the software (android app)... This leaves a lot to be desired. Very little customization. Weak detection often misses people. The alert system is extremely basic. Like... it's bad. I literally can't speak enough about all the seemingly bare bones features it lacks. Mind you, I'm not expecting much here. But I should be able to set a detection area that sends me alerts for people (not every car rolling through the neighborhood) within it. I should be able to set a smaller detection area that alerts me LOUDLY on my google home devices if a person is detected during certain hours. I should be able to access the camera (security) when connected to a VPN. I should be able to customize the notification tones on my phone. I should be able to access all of this from a website on a web browser, not just my phone. I could go on and on for days about how basic and devoid of features the software is. Just a few "if this, then this" options would go a long way. But honestly the worst part of all is that today I discovered that the annual subscription price for the "Cam Plus" features... is per device. That's right, it's $20 (seems reasonable at first), PER CAMERA. I can overlook the poor software and hope that these basic features become available in the future, but the per camera subscription fee is enough to make me say with certainty: DON'T BUY THIS. A flat annual subscription fee should be an incentive to purchase more cameras. I rarely write bad reviews, but I'm honestly very disappointed in this.

title: Outstanding camera and system!
content: I have been with Wyze since day one and they have always made fantastic products for a very low price and the Wyzecam V3 is no different. The resolution, low light capabilities, night vision and features are far superior to the V2 cameras that I have loved for years. I currently have 20 cameras for various uses including home security, to monitor our dog while we are not at home, I have one on each of my 3D printers to monitor my prints and I have 2 at my elderly mother in laws house to keep an eye on her. The V3 is simply amazing in its capabilities. The Wyze App is extremely easy to use and there are no fees for the basic operation of the system although you can purchase a subscription for enhanced AI detection. Installation could not be easier and the instructions in the app are very easy to follow. YOU MUST USE 2.4GHZ WiFi, it will not work on a 5.8ghz WiFi. You simply follow the app and it will create a QR code on your phone, simply point the camera at the QR code and it will do the rest. You get 2 weeks of revolving storage. It will record 12 seconds of video and put it on the AWS server and it will stay for 2 weeks, replacing older video with newer events. If you want to record more than 12 seconds you can either subscribe, or, the better option is to install up to a 32gb Micro SD card and set it to continuously record. You can record the 12 second alert video, then switch to playback mode to watch the rest of the video. The night vision is amazing and it has unbelievable low light capabilities as well. You can set it to do time lapse as well. You can set motion zones, customize alerts, and it has a built in siren that you can either trigger manually, or set it up to sound the alarm when the camera is triggered. For under $40, you really can't go wrong. Oh, it also has a feature that will send an alert to your phone if it hears your smoke or CO2 detectors. Built in microphone and speaker allows you to talk to and listen to the subject. The pictures I have included in the review show the low light, night vision and daytime video (note the time stamp in the lower right). Time stamp, Wyze logo can be turned off in the app and the camera can be rotated if you need to mount the camera under an eve. The V3 is also water proof and can be mounted outside. Another great Wyze product is the Wyze Doorbell, check it out! Wyze also has a spotlight that mounts an the camera and can also be controlled remotely, or it can be triggered automatically.

It's like it disregards my 1hr interval request and have not been able to get any successful time laps longer than a day using the schedule feature.  I hope a future firmware update fixes this issue but for me personally removes half this items usefulness/reason I purchased them.

The mounting system on the bottom of the camera takes a minute for you to get the right position, but it does also include a couple adaptors for various situations, plus the camera itself has a threaded hole in the bottom for a more traditional mount, should you choose. Overall, I would not hesitate buying a couple more, along with some micro SD cards and USB extension cables.  I can't wait for them to make the V3 a pan and tilt exterior camera.

The only events still saved on the cloud for the prior 5 days (since upgrading from the free trial to the annual subscription) were from about 8:30 PM to just after 10:00 PM. After an extremely poorly handled and long call with customer service during which I was told I needed a sim card to record events (retracted after a long hold), I was instructed to provide a log to their engineers. title: Highly recommended!
content: I got the wyze camv3 and couldn't be happier with it, especially for the price! You have the option to subscribe to cam plus monitoring for a reasonable annual price per camera which I recommend.  If you don't want to,  you don't have to. Difference with the service is the time recording. Without, it only records short 12 sec videos every 5 minutes. However, you still have a continuous live stream. The night vision is awesome and the outdoor starlight vision is absolutely amazing!!!! The only feature I would like this to have is the pan, but have found it is not really necessary where I have them installed. There is a pan cam available for a higher price, but I found it to be too big for my purposes.  My son has one and is pretty happy with it for his intended use. These are a wired version, meaning they just plug into any outlet, which I like so I don't have to mess with charging or batteries.  I also have the wyze doorbell cam as well and like it a lot too. All so far were easy to install and set up with the wyze cam app you download on your smartphone  or computer,  available for ios and Android. Requires 2g home internet network and you can view from anywhere you are, on your smartphone or computer. The only annoyance I have had with this is when a bunny rabbit   kept crossing back and forth over my driveway.  I was getting an alert every 2-3 minutes in the early dawn hours that kept waking me up. So I readjusted my sensitivity settings and and alerts for only people and vehicles.  I turned off the motion settings as well cause it would go off if my trees branches blew in the wind. Still, super happy and highly recommended.  I have had these installed for several months now, with no issues.

It also only records about 24 hours of 1080p video on the 32 GB card, anything older will not be saved and will be automatically erased without cloud storage. My last complaint is the limited options for viewing the live feed and playback, the only way to view the video is by using the Wyze app on an Android or Apple device. I prefer to view the video on a Windows device and had to download an Android emulator (Nox Player) to watch the video on my PC laptop. There should be a login website or free windows store app that allows customers to watch their videos on any device and not have to download additional software. I will be buying a different brand security camera soon mostly because this thing is no good, think it will be used to watch my fridge from now on. Lol

title: Great and easy to set up
content: The first thing is first, ensure your mobile device is set to use the 2.4Ghz antenna on your home router or it wont connect. If you want to move the camera, unplug it, move it, and plug it in. It will work as long as its in range of your wifi router. If you dont want to use Wyze server service, buy a SD card and insert the SD into the bottom of the camera, the camera will save the video and delete the oldest first once it fills up. Motion capture is excellent! night vision is very very good for such a small device at this price point! and the image quality for $35 is honestly Very good as well. Just like majority of Wifi cameras they do suffer from light buffering where the Live Feed lags or skips a frame for a split second every now and then but overall for a Wifi Camera its performance is really good! I would strongly recommend the Wyze 3 for anyone looking for a Cheap Outdoor water proof Camera. I don't think there is anything better you can buy for $35.

The white sticks out like a sore eye. The other thing that was the not appealing to me was that this has the WORST zoom capability out of all the cameras I tested. The other cameras where able to pick up the address across the street or a license plate across the street. The Wyze camera barely even zooms in to my front yard. Very very very disappointing. The software is also not user friendly. It's hard to find where your recordings are. You get an alarm but NO Events. Hmmm therefore you try to go back and view the recording and it says NO Events. Yet my notifications are there indicating that there was movement. Once I clear my phone notification there's NO way to find it in the software. Also the camera doesn't seem to focus as it's a following a target. Example. I have the camera in front of my window. I walk outside and back. The camera picks me up but as I get closer it doesn't continue to focus onmy face. I could never use these cameras for evidence as the Police wouldn't be able to make out a clear face of the person. I really hope Wyze can fix these issues. If so I will be a life time customer but until then I will return these and pass for now.

title: Way better compared to my previous security camera.
content: My previous security camera setup was the Arlo Pro 2. Comparing this Wyze v3 camera with the Arlo Pro 2, I am confident to say that these are way better. There were many problems I had with the Arlo Pro 2 cameras. They were very expensive (more than $100 per cam), very slow to load live footage, and the live footage was very delayed (about 10 seconds delayed). I think that the Wyze V3 solved all of the problems that I had with the Arlo cameras. I live how these cameras are extremely affordable, loads the live footage in seconds and the delay is almost non existent. I think that is mostly thanks to the wired connection. One thing that I do not like about these cameras is that without the cam plus subscription it only records a 12 second clip every 5 minutes. To solve this, I was able to use the sd card slot to it can record 24/7. Comparing the video quality, even though they are both 1080p, the Wyze's colors were more vivid and handled the exposure better. Lastly, the color night vision is pretty amazing. I tested it in my backyard where it is pitch black and I was able to everything in color although it was kind of blurry. If there was ambient light, the picture quality would be better. Overall I was surprised that I can get so much for only $32 compared to my over $100 Arlo cameras.

The CAM PLUS seems to allow for differentiating vehicles and people, but personally I am okay with not having that distinction and just picking up all motion. I am on a budget and this camera seems to satisfy all my needs. The camera quality is good. It is wired for power, and wifi for live streaming (and cloud storage if you do get a subscription). If you want simplicity and are budget minded, then rate this among your options. This also does surprisingly well at night due to some night features with the lighting. Motion detecting is amazing. Catches people, cars, and bikes but not the leaves moving on my tree. You can set the sensitivity in the app (I use it at 50%). You can also do sound detection. I disabled this feature so I can't report on it's sensitivity, sorry.  This will help keep an eye on the drug dealers and rising crime that seems to be creeping up.
